Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes): New severe headache for 3 days with photophobia and intermittent visual phenomena ("shooting lights"). No chronic illnesses reported. No documented hypertension or diabetes.  
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes): Mother with severe migraines (with vomiting). No other family history recorded.  
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines: Combined oral contraceptive pill — dose/route/frequency not documented. Ibuprofen intermittently for headache — dose/route/frequency not documented. Paracetamol recommended by clinician — dose/route/frequency not documented. Clinician stated they could prescribe a "stronger" analgesic — medication name/dose/route/frequency not documented. No traditional/herbal medicines recorded.  
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus): Not recorded.  
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks: On combined oral contraceptive pill started ~1 year ago. Clinician noted that if recurrent migraine with aura is confirmed the pill may need review; instructed to continue for now. No pregnancy status or STI screening recorded.  
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use: Non-smoker. Alcohol: patient reports drinking approximately once weekly ("three, once a week"). No recreational drug use reported. Physical activity and diet not documented.  
- Hearing and vision concerns: Photophobia and intermittent visual phenomena ("shooting lights") associated with headache. Patient reports recent eye check with "nothing changed." No hearing concerns reported.  
- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm): Reports some lack of energy attributed to headache. No history or symptoms of depression, anxiety, or self-harm documented.  
- Social context: family support, caregiving, housing, financial stressors: Lives alone. Works from home; has missed/limited work due to headache (took a day off and reduced work capability). No other social or financial stressors recorded.

Examination

- Vital signs: BP, pulse rate and rhythm: Not recorded. Patient reports pharmacy BP check ~1 year ago was "normal."  
- Anthropometry: height, weight, BMI, waist circumference if indicated: Not recorded.  
- Oral health: gums, teeth, dentures if relevant: Not recorded.  
- Ear exam including otoscopy: Not recorded.  
- Eye exam: visual acuity, pupil response, fundus if indicated: No documented exam. Patient reports recent eye check with no change. Clinician planned neurological examination and fundoscopy at face-to-face appointment.  
- Urinalysis: dipstick for protein, glucose, ketones, blood: Not recorded.

- Blood tests: fasting glucose and lipids preferred; HbA1c if diabetes present/suspected: Not recorded.  
- Renal function and liver function tests if clinically indicated: Not recorded.  
- ECG if cardiac risk factors present or baseline: Not recorded.  
- Cervical screening if eligible and due: Not recorded.  
- Mammography if eligible and not up to date: Not recorded.  
- Faecal occult blood test if due: Not recorded.  
- Bone density (DEXA) if osteoporosis risk present: Not recorded.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key clinical findings and impressions:
  - Acute/subacute severe headache for 3 days, sudden onset on waking, continuous with partial relief from ibuprofen (pain reported ~8/10 down to ~5/10). Pain generalized but worse over right eye. Photophobia and intermittent "shooting lights" (visual phenomena). No nausea/vomiting (only "feeling a bit sick"), no sensory loss, weakness, or change in smell/taste. Sleeps reasonably well and not woken by headache. Lives alone; mother with migraine.
  - Clinician assessment in transcript: possible migraine; planned face-to-face neurological exam and fundoscopy; advised expedited review if worsening; offered a stronger analgesic and paracetamol for symptomatic relief; advised continuing oral contraceptive for now but review if migraine with aura is confirmed.
  - DDx supports migraine with visual aura as most likely; DDx also raises concern for cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) and idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) as medium-probability secondary causes given OCP use and persistent headache. Subarachnoid hemorrhage considered less likely but not excluded.
- Working diagnosis: Probable migraine (migraine with visual phenomena/aura). Rationale: photophobia, subjective visual phenomena, family history of migraine, severe pain partially responsive to analgesia, no systemic or focal neurological signs documented — supported by DDx (High likelihood).
- Considerations from DDx (additional plausible but uncertain options):
  - Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) — Medium likelihood: young woman on combined oral contraceptive; subacute progressive headache and visual symptoms may fit; requires imaging to exclude.  
  - Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) — Medium likelihood: persistent headache with visual disturbance in a young woman; fundoscopy needed to evaluate for papilledema.  
  - Subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) — Low likelihood but consider if sudden thunderclap characteristics or any worsening/new neurological signs.
- Immediate plan and actions from transcript consistent with DDx:
  - Arrange in-person appointment for full neurological examination, blood pressure check, and fundoscopy as planned by clinician.  
  - Symptomatic treatment offered: clinician to prescribe a stronger analgesic in place of ibuprofen (medication name/dose/route/frequency not documented) and advised paracetamol concurrently (dose/route/frequency not documented). Take with food as advised.  
  - Continue combined oral contraceptive for now; clinician will reassess if migraines with aura are established.  
  - Safety net: patient advised to attend Emergency Department if headache becomes unbearable, worse, or if new/worsening neurological symptoms occur.  
  - Consider urgent neuroimaging (non-contrast CT head ± CT venography or MRI/MRV) if any red flags arise (sudden severe peak pain, focal deficits, seizures, progressive symptoms, papilledema) — imaging not performed/recorded in transcript.  
  - Consider referral to neurology or headache clinic if symptoms persist or secondary causes not excluded on initial exam/imaging.

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification: Not recorded beyond clinician advice to continue pill for now and to take prescribed analgesia with food. No documented education on migraine triggers, sleep hygiene, hydration, or analgesic-overuse prevention.  
- Patient health goals and priorities: Not recorded explicitly; patient requested information about specialist referral and agreed to face-to-face assessment.  
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA): Not recorded.  
- Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports): Face-to-face appointment with support team arranged/requested; no other referrals documented.  
- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled: Face-to-face examination to be booked via support team; no date recorded. Safety net advice to present to ED if worsening.

Consider

- Mental health support or counselling referral: Not recorded.  
- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management: Neurology/headache clinic referral considered if persistent symptoms or abnormal findings — not yet arranged.  
- Dental referral if oral health issues identified: Not recorded.  
- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening: Not recorded; fundoscopy planned at in-person exam.  
- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected: Not recorded.  
- Social work or housing support referral if social determinants affect health: Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Migraine (probable migraine with visual aura) — High. Justification: Photophobia, intermittent visual phenomena ("shooting lights"), family history of migraine, severe headache interfering with function, partial response to analgesia; no focal neurological signs or fever documented.  
- Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) — Medium. Justification: Patient is on combined oral contraceptive (increased thrombotic risk); subacute progressive headache with visual symptoms; positional/stabbing element reported when moving head; requires imaging to exclude.  
- Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) — Medium. Justification: Young woman with persistent headache and visual disturbances; IIH can present similarly and requires fundoscopy/imaging to assess for papilledema and raised intracranial pressure.

Quality checks
- Missing but clinically expected elements: Vital signs (BP, pulse), neurological examination findings, fundoscopy/papilledema assessment, any neuroimaging (CT/MRI), blood tests (including infection/ inflammatory markers), immunisation review, explicit medication names/doses for prescribed analgesia, and patient identifying details (name/DOB) not documented in transcript.  
- Internal conflicts or contradictions between transcript and DDx: None substantive; DDx lists a range of secondary causes to consider which are consistent with clinician's plan to perform neurological exam/fundoscopy and to escalate if red flags present.  
- Transcript quality notes: Initial audio volume issues noted at start; patient name/DOB/home address not captured in transcript. Some patient responses truncated/ellipses present. Medication details sparse (oral contraceptive type/name not specified; analgesic prescribed unnamed).
